main_text.l: ne fumendus: stomachus oleo absynthite,
cui addita sit nardi spica, aut celtica robo-
randus. Quod si diuturnus iam sit factus
morb. & per essentiam arq; proprietatem,
tunc cauftica duo fiant: unum, quod sit in-
fra uentriculum, ut in crure: alterum in sca-
pula, prius uapores auertet: posterius è ce-
rebro humores deriuabit. Si ob menfium
aut fecundæ retentionem, obortta sit epile-
psia, curabitur medicamentis aperientibus,
ut pulegii, calaminthæ, origani, sabinæ ru-
tæ, arthemisiæ, radicis Aristolochiæ longę,
aut rotundæ, decoctis, fotibus & iniectio-
nibus, Trochiscis è myrrha, pesis ex hiera
mellita, cui myrrhæ nonnihil additum sit.
Secundam quoq; deturbant sternutamen-
ta naribus subdita, tefte Hippocrate, Apho-
rismo quadragesimo nono, Sectionis quin-
tæ. Ad lecudas[?] deturbandas sternutario im-
misso nares, & os manu obturat. Poterit
quoq; purgari corpus pilulis, quæ uterum
expurgant, ut fœtidis & de agarico. A' pur-
gatione non parum conferunt theriaca, mi-
thridatium, & triphera magna sine opio.
Nam his remediis omnibus profligari po-
terit comitialis morbus à feminis corru-
ptione natus. Qui uero prægnanti contin-gic[?]

page.notes: Catchword "gic" is partly cut at the edge of the scan and is a fragment of the next word. The first word of the second paragraph, "lecudas", is probably "fecundas" in the printer's type but is marked as doubtful. Printed spellings such as "pulegij", "remedijs" and "uero" were normalised for i/j and u/v; "longę", "quoq;" and "A'" are kept as printed. The paragraph break before "Secundam" follows the short line ending "additum sit." The text runs on into the catchword line.
